QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_20

question.text: A cash-futures arbitrageur buys a government bond at Rs. 99.50 in the spot market and simultaneously sells a 3-month futures at Rs. 101.20. The 3-month financing cost is Rs. 0.80 and expected coupon accrual is Rs. 0.30. What is the arbitrage profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures price equals cash price plus financing cost minus income on the cash position (workbook pp. 126-127). Net cost of carry = 0.80 - 0.30 = Rs. 0.50, so fair futures = 99.50 + 0.50 = 100.00. Arbitrage profit = 101.20 - 100.00 = Rs. 1.20. Equivalently: 101.20 - 99.50 - 0.80 + 0.30 = Rs. 1.20. The Trap: Rs. 1.70 ignores financing cost (101.20 - 99.50). Rs. 0.90 ignores coupon. Rs. 1.50 double-counts an item. Note: When futures trade above the theoretical futures price, regular arbitrage is to buy the underlying bond and sell futures (workbook pp. 187-188).
